name: v100
description: NVIDIA Tesla V100 SXM2 (GV100, Volta, sm_70) at its 1530 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 80 SMs, 64 resident warps/SM, 4 processing blocks with one scheduler each (NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 1)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 6 MB L2 (whitepaper): 24 ways over power-of-two sets, 32 banks for the 32 memory channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 4 HBM2 stacks x 8 128-bit channels = 32 channels at 1752 MT/s: 32 x 16 B x 1752 MT/s = 897 GB/s (whitepaper)
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock; lanes reading one 8 B word share its bank access, so a stride-1 FP32 warp read is conflict-free as on the part
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (TFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Volta tensor cores: FP16 inputs with FP32 accumulation only (Volta whitepaper). The TCU's FP16 format group also carries BF16, which Volta lacks: no knob separates them
sources.TCU_PE_RATIO: 512 dense FP16 FMA per clock per SM: 8 tensor cores of 64 FMA each (NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper; 125 TFLOPS at 1530 MHz over 80 SMs). A TCU block at NUM_THREADS=32 computes an 8x4x4-word tile, 256 FP16 FMA per clock, so the 4 blocks give 1024: ratio 2
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Raster engines in every GPC and ROPs in every memory partition (architecture whitepaper)
sources.NUM_TFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 7.0)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GV100 SM (Volta whitepaper, Figure 5): 4 processing blocks, each with 16 FP32, 16 INT32, 8 FP64 cores, 8 LD/ST units, 1 SFU and 2 tensor cores. One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block (ISSUE_WIDTH=4) with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes; a 32-thread warp instruction issues over NUM_THREADS/lanes cycles, as on the part. The TCU stays full-warp (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS). FP64 FMAs run on their own F64 FMA PEs (FMA64_PE_RATIO)
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at half the FP32 rate: 8 FP64 against 16 FP32 cores per processing block (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 7.0); 16 FPU lanes / 2 = 8 F64 FMA PEs. FP64 division, square root and conversions take the FDIV/FSQRT/FCVT rates
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 4 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput); 16 FPU lanes / 4, compute capability 7.0
sources.DCACHE_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock of L1 data per SM: 4 banks of the 32 B dcache word. The default (one bank per LSU request channel) gives 8, twice the part (Volta whitepaper: 128 B/clk L1)
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 96 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 7.0) in a 128 KB window. DCACHE_SIZE keeps the whole 128 KB L1/shared pool: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves, so a kernel without shared memory sees the full pool
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Volta GPU Architecture via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1804.06826), Figure 3.2: L1 hit 28, L2 hit 193, L2 miss with a TLB hit 375 cycles
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 65 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network, which the L2 bank pipeline (L2_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 193-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 88 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the L2 link, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 375-cycle global memory latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 64 per bank: Little's law on the L2-miss round trip ci/profile_check.py measures (DRAM 375 - L2 hit 193 = 182 cycles) x 588 B/cycle (900 GB/s / 1530 MHz) / (32 banks x 64 B) = 52.3, rounded up to a power of two. The derived default counts only PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, which the link latency now mostly replaces
